params_note: Summed across the TP group with xm.all_reduce, so these are whole-model counts rather than this rank's shard. Parameters that are replicated rather than sharded (norms, LoRA A/B on replicated modules) are counted once per rank and so are marginally over-counted -- under 0.01% for an 8B model.

config.device_note: trn1.2xlarge: 1x Trainium1, 2x NeuronCore-v2, 32 GiB HBM (16 GiB per core) at 820 GB/s. 190 TFLOP/s BF16 per chip (arch page); 210 under the instance-derived convention.

holdout.note: Held-out in-domain token loss on rows never trained on. Supports 'the fine-tune learned, comparably on both chips'. Does NOT support any claim about instruction quality or downstream benchmarks.

first_step_note: Step 1 traces the XLA graph and then either compiles it or loads it from the NEFF cache. A warm cache (lane 3 precompile) collapses this toward the median; a cold cache leaves tens of minutes in it.
throughput_note: tokens_per_s is steady-state (median step, warmup excluded); tokens_per_s_end_to_end divides ALL tokens by the full training wall clock. measured_window_fraction is what share of wall time the median-step window actually covers. Compare like with like.
peak_bf16_flops_source: Neuron arch page arch/neuron-hardware/trainium: 190 FP16/BF16/cFP8/TF32 TFLOPS per chip
peak_bf16_flops_alt_source: trn1.32xlarge marketed at 3.4 PFLOP/s / 16 devices = 212.5, rounded to 210 -- the denominator behind every published Phase-1/2 MFU
peak_device_mem_note: Device HBM high-water is not available from torch on XLA. Read it from the matching telemetry CSV (mem_used_mib column, sampled at 1 Hz by neuron-monitor). Deliberately null rather than estimated.
